issues.problem: The copy narrates the teacher instead of stating the ideas, the same voice problem as lec01 #14. Examples: 'The instructor's view is blunt: ORMs suck, and he hates them', 'he has scaled SQL systems massively', 'which is why the instructor is a big supporter of formal education', 'the instructor expects IRCTC's code base to be full of skip locks … That is his inference', 'the instructor went through its source code', 'by his estimate', 'The instructor agreed'. Chapter 6 reads as a biography.
issues.fix: Keep provenance in the meta lines and in figure captions. Rewrite the claims as plain statements, marking opinions once ('An opinion, not a rule:'). Drop the teacher's career details (his scaling history, source-code reading, formal-education view) or fold them into one 'From class' aside. Keep the ORM verdict as a stated trade-off, not as 'he hates them'.

issues.problem: This is a figure desert. Five desktop screens (about eight on phone) of unbroken paragraphs run from the chapter opening to Fig 6·a, with no figure, card, key-rule box or aside. This breaks the sample's paragraph–figure–paragraph rhythm.
issues.fix: Cut chapter 6 prose by about 30% (see C-02). Add one figure for the ORM section: a small two-panel 'ORM chain vs one SQL statement' sheet (e.g. a 10-table join as an ORM call chain beside the SQL), or a key-rule box 'Write the big queries in SQL'. Put a sticky-note card or a short list in §6.3 'How to learn this' (read the source for a week · read the official docs · the CS basics recur).

issues.problem: Collapsed asides stack with a blank band of about 50px between each rule pair, so three closed '+' rows ('From your OS course', 'Why the index matters', 'A debugging hunch') take a third of a screen and look like broken empty boxes. Each sits straight after the previous one with no prose between, which is the 'stack of components' the sample avoids.
issues.fix: Remove the empty body/margin a closed <details> renders (collapse its content box to 0 height when closed). Allow at most two asides back to back; move the third next to the paragraph it qualifies, or fold it in.

issues.problem: Arrows are on the wrong side. In panel a, the green SKIP LOCKED arrows point from rows 3 and 4 into T2, but T2 is the initiator.
